intent: Investigate whether this session's work caused the 2026-08-22 11:33 hard freeze, and bound the one unbounded thing the coverage jail could do regardless of the verdict.
scope: meta/scripts/shell_coverage_jail.sh: per-case timeout and stdin closed
Non-goal: changing anything else about the jail; the freeze investigation cleared it
changes: Each kcov case now runs under `timeout --kill-after=10s` with a default 120s ceiling, overridable with --timeout.
Each case runs with stdin redirected from /dev/null, so a subject that reads stdin cannot block on the caller's terminal.
A timed-out case prints a warning naming the case, rather than being swallowed by the existing `|| true`.

verification.command: journalctl --list-boots; journalctl -b -1 for OOM, hung tasks, lockups and late kernel messages
verification.result: pass - this session's work is not implicated
verification.evidence: Boot -1 ended 11:33:15 with the log cut mid-line. No OOM kill, no oom_reaper, no hung-task or soft-lockup message anywhere, and NO kernel message at all after 11:20 -- a hard hang signature rather than a process the kernel was fighting.

verification.command: correlate this session's activity with the final minutes of boot -1
verification.result: pass - the session was idle when the freeze happened
verification.evidence: Last commit 11:30:32; last system-level trace from a jail run at 11:11:57 (a failed sudo from an early attempt), over 21 minutes before the freeze. Meanwhile Steam wrote a crash minidump at 11:31:10 and at-spi2 disabled an unresponsive app (pid 4848) at 11:32:06, on an RTX 3090 with the proprietary driver.

verification.command: ps for unshare/kcov; ls /tmp/tmp.*; mount | grep /tmp/tmp.; stat the live system files
verification.result: pass - no residue survived the reboot
verification.evidence: No stray processes, no leftover jail tmpdirs, zero leaked mounts. /etc/modules-load.d/night-lockdown-i2c.conf still dated 2026-07-23 and /usr/local/bin/sync-dot-cert.sh still dated 2026-08-11, both untouched.

verification.result: pass - no regression from the timeout change
verification.evidence: dot_resolver_install.sh: 39/39 lines = 100.00%, both before and after.

verification.command: run a subject whose body is `sleep 600` with --timeout 5s
verification.evidence: 'warn: case timed out after 5s' and the whole run finished in 5 seconds instead of 600.
Clean, no suppressions; the file is exactly at the 250-line cap.

risks: The freeze cause is NOT positively identified. A hard hang leaves no log by construction, so the Steam minidump two minutes prior is a correlation, not a proven cause. What is established is the negative: nothing from this session was running at the time, and no OOM occurred.

The jail still runs real installers as uid 0 inside a namespace. That is the most invasive thing this tooling does, and while containment was verified by canary, escape assertion and mtime checks, it remains the part with any plausible blast radius.
The 120s default is a guess, not a measured figure. A legitimately slow suite could now be cut off; the warning names the case so that failure is visible rather than silent.
rollback: git revert this commit; the jail returns to unbounded per-case execution.
After rollback, confirm dot_resolver_install.sh still measures 39/39 through the runner.
